The countries of origin for U.S. cell imports differ substantially from the global distribution of c- Si cell production (Figure 5) owing to tariff and AD/CVD considerations. Imported cells from South Korea would have some of the lowest duties, and the largest c-Si module assembly firm in the United States (Qcells) is headquartered in that country. Quarterly shipments from Q3 2024 to Q1 2025 have remained relatively flat at around 4 GW . dc As growing U.S. module assembly operations increased demand for cells in 2024, the U.S. cell tariff rate quota was surpassed. The tariff rate quota allows duty-free cells until the total volume of imports into the United States exceeds a certain capacity per year (with the year starting February 7 and ending February 6 of the next calendar year).
